mission.name: The Nameless Chart
mission.description:
The web team handed over their first Helm chart, `webapp`, and went on holiday.
Every attempt to install it dies immediately:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: validation: chart.metadata.version is required
Nothing reaches the cluster. The chart lives in your workspace under `webapp/`.
mission.objective:
Release `webapp` is deployed in namespace `helmissions` from the chart in your
workspace (chart version 0.1.0), its 2 nginx pods are Ready, and `helm lint`
passes for the chart.

mission.name: Name Rejected
mission.description:
The shop team's pipeline script `deploy.sh` stopped the Friday release cold. It runs
`helm install Shop_Frontend ./storefront` and Helm answers:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: release name check failed: release name "Shop_Frontend":
  invalid release name, must match regex ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]...
The storefront chart itself is fine; nothing is deployed.
mission.objective:
`deploy.sh` in your workspace runs successfully and leaves release `shop-frontend` deployed
in namespace `helmissions` from the storefront chart, with its 2 pods Ready. The script itself
must use a release name that Helm accepts, so the next pipeline run works too.

mission.name: Pull Backoff
mission.description:
The `ledger-api` release was installed from the chart in your workspace and Helm reports it as
`deployed`, yet nobody can reach the API. `kubectl get pods -n helmissions` shows the pods stuck in
`ErrImagePull` / `ImagePullBackOff`, and `kubectl describe pod` ends with
  Failed to pull image "nginx:1.27-alpien": ... manifest unknown
mission.objective:
Release `ledger-api` in namespace `helmissions` runs 2 Ready pods using image
`nginx:1.27-alpine`. The chart in your workspace (`ledger-api/values.yaml`) carries the correct
tag, and the release recorded by Helm uses it - a patch on the live Deployment alone is not enough.

mission.name: The Empty Release
mission.description:
The logistics team installed `parcel-tracker` and Helm printed a cheerful
  STATUS: deployed
  DESCRIPTION: Install complete
but the tracking page is unreachable. `helm list` shows the release, `kubectl get all -n helmissions`
shows nothing at all - no pods, no Deployment, no Service. There was no error anywhere.
mission.objective:
Release `parcel-tracker` in namespace `helmissions` is deployed from the chart in your workspace and
its Helm manifest contains a Deployment and a Service. The pod is Ready and the Service has an
endpoint. The resources must be owned by the Helm release (not applied by hand).

mission.name: Required Means Required
mission.description:
The docs team's chart refuses to install the staging portal:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: execution error at (docs-site/templates/ingress.yaml:9:21):
  ingressHost is required: set the public host name of the docs portal
The chart is shared with other environments, so its defaults must stay generic. `README.txt` in your
workspace lists the staging settings.
mission.objective:
Release `docs-site` is deployed in namespace `helmissions` with the staging host from `README.txt`
(`docs.staging.helmissions.local`) on its Ingress and its pod Ready. The host is supplied through a
values file in your workspace (next to the chart, not inside it); the chart's own `values.yaml`
still has no host hardcoded.

mission.name: Chart.yml Is Not Chart.yaml
mission.description:
A contractor delivered the `status-page` chart and Helm will not even look at it:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: unable to detect chart at .../status-page/Chart.yaml:
  open .../status-page/Chart.yaml: no such file or directory
`helm lint` says the same. Yet the chart folder clearly contains a metadata file with the right
contents, and the templates look fine.
mission.objective:
Release `status-page` (chart version 0.2.0 from your workspace) is deployed in namespace
`helmissions` and serves its HTML page. The chart folder in your workspace contains the correctly named
metadata file and no leftover misnamed copy; `helm lint` passes.

mission.name: Connection Refused
mission.description:
Callers of the `inventory` service get errors. The release is deployed, both pods are Ready and
`kubectl get endpoints inventory -n helmissions` lists two addresses - the Service looks perfectly healthy.
Yet a request from another pod fails:
  curl: (7) Failed to connect to inventory.helmissions.svc port 80: Connection refused
mission.objective:
A request to `http://inventory.helmissions.svc/` from inside the cluster returns HTTP 200.
The fix must be part of the Helm release (revision recorded by Helm) and of the chart in your
workspace, so a later `helm upgrade` does not break it again.

mission.name: Nowhere To Land
mission.description:
Ticket OPS-2217 (see `TICKET.txt`) asks for release `metrics-proxy` in the new staging namespace
`helmissions-staging`. The install dies immediately:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: create: failed to create: namespaces "helmissions-staging" not found
The chart is fine - it simply has nowhere to land.
mission.objective:
Release `metrics-proxy` is deployed in namespace `helmissions-staging` (and not in `helmissions`)
from the chart in your workspace; its pod is Ready and the Service has an endpoint.

mission.name: Cannot Re-use a Name
mission.description:
Release `orders` (chart 0.1.0) has been serving the shop since last month. The workspace now holds
the new chart, `orders` 0.2.0, and the rollout command fails:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: release name check failed: cannot reuse a name that is still in use
(Helm 3 spells it "cannot re-use a name that is still in use".) Last time somebody "solved" this
by deleting the release, and nobody could roll back when the deploy went wrong.
mission.objective:
Release `orders` in namespace `helmissions` runs chart `orders-0.2.0` from your workspace with 2 Ready
pods and the new `orders-config` ConfigMap. Its revision history still contains the original 0.1.0
revision - the release must not have been deleted and recreated.

mission.name: The Silent --set
mission.description:
Before the month-end run a colleague scaled `billing` with
  helm upgrade billing ./billing --set replicacount=4 -n helmissions
Helm answered `Release "billing" has been upgraded. Happy Helming!` and revision 2 is deployed,
yet `kubectl get pods` still shows a single worker. No error, no warning.
mission.objective:
Release `billing` in namespace `helmissions` runs 4 Ready worker pods because its user-supplied values
contain `replicaCount: 4`. The wrongly-cased `replicacount` key must no longer be part of the release's
values. Scaling the Deployment by hand does not count.

mission.name: The Mystery Override
mission.description:
Since yesterday's deploy the weather widget on the portal shows "Could not reach weather service".
The chart in your workspace has not changed in weeks and its defaults are correct, and the release
is `deployed` with a Ready pod. Something about the way `weather-widget` was deployed is different
from what is in git (see `NOTE-from-support.txt`).
mission.objective:
Release `weather-widget` in namespace `helmissions` has no user-supplied `config.apiUrl`, and its
ConfigMap `weather-widget-config` carries the chart's default API URL. The fix must be recorded in the
Helm release itself - editing the live ConfigMap does not count. Do not change the chart files.

mission.name: Read The Label
mission.description:
The monitoring team got a vendor chart as a single file, `vendor/node-probe-0.4.2.tgz`: no source
repository, no documentation page, only the archive. Ticket `TICKET.txt` asks for release `node-probe` whose Service
listens on port 9100 instead of the default. Nobody knows which value controls the port, and the
last attempt `--set service.port=9100` installed fine but the Service still listens on 80.
mission.objective:
Release `node-probe` (chart `node-probe-0.4.2` from the packaged archive) is deployed in namespace
`helmissions` and its Service listens on port 9100 and answers requests there. The setting is kept in
`probe-values.yaml` in your workspace and that file was used for the install.

mission.name: Not Every File Is A Manifest
mission.description:
The helpdesk chart came with a friendly file of operator notes, and now it cannot be installed at all:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: YAML parse error on helpdesk/templates/usage-notes.yaml:
  error converting YAML to JSON: yaml: line 6: mapping values are not allowed in this context
`helm lint` reports the same file. The Deployment, Service and ConfigMap templates are fine.
mission.objective:
Release `helpdesk` is deployed in namespace `helmissions` from the chart in your workspace; the Deployment,
Service and ConfigMap are rendered, every rendered document is a real Kubernetes manifest, and the pod
is Ready. The operator notes may be kept, but not as a manifest-looking file in `templates/`.

mission.name: Lint Before You Ship
mission.description:
The CI pipeline for the `newsletter` chart is red. Its only gate is `ci/lint.sh`, which runs
`helm lint --strict ./newsletter` and ends with
  Error: 1 chart(s) linted, 1 chart(s) failed
The output mixes [ERROR], [WARNING] and [INFO] lines about the chart's metadata and the objects it
creates. Nobody has deployed this chart yet.
mission.objective:
`ci/lint.sh` passes (`helm lint --strict ./newsletter` reports 0 failed charts). The chart is still called
`newsletter`, has a valid SemVer chart version, and still renders the same resources (ConfigMap, Deployment,
Service with the same image). Release `newsletter` is then installed in namespace `helmissions` from the fixed
chart and its pod is Ready. A missing icon is only an INFO message and may stay.

mission.name: Ship A Clean Package
mission.description:
The `reports` chart (version 1.1.0) must be released through the artifact repository, which picks up
`dist/*.tgz`. See `RELEASE-NOTES.txt`. The working copy of the chart contains files that only exist on
a developer's machine, and `helm package` bundles everything it finds in the chart directory. A security
review already bounced an earlier archive.
mission.objective:
`dist/reports-1.1.0.tgz` exists in your workspace and contains only chart files - no `secrets.local.env`,
no `*.bak` files and no `tmp/` directory. Release `reports` is deployed in namespace `helmissions` from
that package (chart version 1.1.0) and its pod is Ready.

mission.name: A Path Is Not A File
mission.description:
A colleague deployed the marketing site as release `landing` with
`helm install landing ./landing --set siteConfig=./site.conf`, expecting Helm to read
the file. The release says `deployed`, but the nginx pod never becomes Ready and keeps
restarting. `kubectl logs` shows an nginx configuration error, and the ConfigMap that
should hold the server block looks suspiciously short.
mission.objective:
Release `landing` in namespace `helmissions` is deployed and its nginx pod is Ready.
The ConfigMap `landing-nginx` (key `default.conf`) must contain exactly the contents
of `site.conf` from your workspace, delivered through Helm (not patched by hand), and
the site must answer on the `landing` Service with the page text from `site.conf`.

mission.name: "false" Is True
mission.description:
The platform team says the storefront must not be exposed through an Ingress: traffic
arrives via the API gateway. `storefront/values.yaml` even says `ingress.enabled: "false"`.
Yet release `storefront` keeps creating an Ingress, and `kubectl get ingress -n helmissions`
shows `storefront` with host `shop.example.com`. Deleting it by hand only works until the
next deploy.
mission.objective:
Release `storefront` in namespace `helmissions` is deployed with 1 ready pod and its
manifest contains no Ingress, and no Ingress exists in the namespace. The computed value
`ingress.enabled` must be a real boolean `false`, and the fix must come through Helm
(an Ingress removed with kubectl does not count).

mission.name: Nil Pointer In The Cache Block
mission.description:
`profile-svc` deploys fine to production, where the values file carries a `cache.redis`
block. The staging deploy (`./deploy-staging.sh`, which uses `values-staging.yaml`) has no
cache layer, and Helm refuses to render:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: profile-svc/templates/configmap.yaml:...
    executing "profile-svc/templates/configmap.yaml" at <.Values.cache.redis.host>:
      nil pointer evaluating interface {}.redis
Nothing is installed in staging.
mission.objective:
The chart renders both without a `cache` block anywhere in the values and with one
(`--set cache.redis.host=...` puts that host into the rendered ConfigMap). Release
`profile-svc` is deployed in namespace `helmissions` from the staging values and its pod is Ready.
Fixing it by adding a dummy cache block only to the staging file is not enough; the chart
itself must cope with the block being absent.

mission.name: Dots In Keys
mission.description:
Prometheus is not scraping the `telemetry-agent` pods. A colleague deployed the release with
`--set podAnnotations.prometheus.io/scrape=true --set podAnnotations.prometheus.io/port=9100`
(see DEPLOY.txt). The release is `deployed`, but when you look at the pod annotations there is
no `prometheus.io/scrape` - there is an odd annotation called `prometheus` instead.
mission.objective:
Release `telemetry-agent` in namespace `helmissions` is deployed and its pod is Ready. The pod
template carries exactly the annotations `prometheus.io/scrape: "true"` and
`prometheus.io/port: "9100"` (as literal keys with dots), and no stray `prometheus` annotation
is left over from the broken deploy.

mission.name: Range Over A String
mission.description:
The `cors-gateway` chart publishes the browser origins allowed to call the public API. The
partner integration team wants to add more origins next week, and the template already loops
over `allowedOrigins`. But right now the release does not even install:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: cors-gateway/templates/configmap.yaml:...
    executing "cors-gateway/templates/configmap.yaml" at <.Values.allowedOrigins>:
      range can't iterate over https://shop.example
mission.objective:
Release `cors-gateway` is deployed in namespace `helmissions` with its pod Ready, and its
ConfigMap `cors-gateway-origins` lists `https://shop.example` as a line in `origins.txt`.
The chart must keep accepting several origins: when a list of origins is supplied, every one
of them appears, one per line.

mission.name: Commas In --set
mission.description:
The network team wants pods of `mesh-client` to resolve short names through two extra DNS
search domains: `payments.svc.cluster.local` and `corp.internal`. The runbook
(`install.sh`) passes them with a single `--set`, and Helm refuses:
  Error: failed parsing --set data: key "internal" has no value
The values must be passed on the command line (no editing the chart's defaults).
mission.objective:
Release `mesh-client` is deployed in namespace `helmissions` and its pod is Ready. The pod's
`dnsConfig.searches` contains exactly the two domains `payments.svc.cluster.local` and
`corp.internal`, delivered through Helm values (the chart template is unchanged in spirit:
`dnsSearch` stays a list).

mission.name: Last One Wins
mission.description:
Production checkout is running with 1 replica and `LOG_LEVEL=debug`, even though
`values-prod.yaml` clearly asks for 3 replicas and `warn` logging. Everyone agrees the
values files are right; the release is deployed by `./deploy.sh` into namespace
`helmissions-prod`. Black Friday is next week.
mission.objective:
Release `checkout` in namespace `helmissions-prod` runs 3 ready replicas with
`LOG_LEVEL=warn`, while the shared setting `REGION=eu-west-1` from `values-base.yaml` is still
applied. `deploy.sh` itself must be fixed (and still deploy `checkout` into `helmissions-prod`
with both values files) so the next pipeline run keeps the result; editing the values files to
hide the problem is not the fix.

mission.name: The Empty Timeout
mission.description:
The `fetcher` release looks healthy in `helm list`, but its pod keeps restarting and
`kubectl logs` says `fetcher: invalid FETCH_TIMEOUT='' (want seconds)`. The rendered
config shows `FETCH_TIMEOUT=` with nothing after the equals sign. Operations says
the timeout was "never meant to be required - 30 seconds has always been the default",
but the chart's `values.yaml` only defines `http.retries`.
mission.objective:
Release `fetcher` in namespace `helmissions` is deployed from the chart in your workspace
and its pod is Ready, with `FETCH_TIMEOUT=30` in the ConfigMap `fetcher-config`.
The chart itself must apply that default whenever `http.timeout` is not provided, and an
explicit `http.timeout` (for example 45) must still be honoured.

mission.name: Invisible Tabs
mission.description:
The compliance team pasted the audit settings from their wiki into `audit-log/values.yaml`
and the chart no longer installs:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: cannot load values.yaml: cannot unmarshal yaml document:
  error converting YAML to JSON: yaml: line 9: found character that cannot start any token
The file looks perfectly aligned in the editor. Line 9 is the first line under `audit:`.
mission.objective:
Release `audit-log` is deployed in namespace `helmissions` with 2 ready pods. `audit-log/values.yaml`
parses as YAML, contains no tab characters, and keeps the intended settings: retention 90 days,
sink `siem.corp.example` on port 6514 with TLS enabled (all served in `audit.conf`).

mission.name: --reuse-values Ate My Default
mission.description:
Chart `notifier` 2.0.0 adds a Prometheus metrics endpoint (`metrics.port`, default 9102 in
`values.yaml`). The CI job (`ci-upgrade.sh`) upgrades the running release with `--reuse-values --set image.tag=1.36`
to keep the settings the team tuned by hand - the release was installed with `--set replicaCount=2`.
The pipeline now fails:
  Error: UPGRADE FAILED: ... executing "notifier/templates/deployment.yaml" at <.Values.metrics.port>:
    nil pointer evaluating interface {}.port
Dropping `--reuse-values` from the job makes the upgrade work, but then the replica count falls back to 1.
mission.objective:
Release `notifier` in namespace `helmissions` runs chart `notifier-2.0.0` and is deployed with
2 ready replicas (the earlier `replicaCount: 2` override is preserved), and the pods expose the
metrics port defined by the new chart's defaults (9102).

mission.name: The Hash That Ate My Password
mission.description:
After the quarterly credential rotation, finance updated `ledger-api/values.yaml` with the new
database password, `Harbor Light #2024`, and redeployed release `ledger-api`. The pod now hangs in
`Init:Error` / `Init:CrashLoopBackOff`; the `auth-check` init container logs
`database rejected the credentials for user ledger`. The DB team swears the new password works.
The password in the values file looks right.
mission.objective:
Release `ledger-api` in namespace `helmissions` is deployed and its pod is Ready (the credential
check passes). The Secret `ledger-api-db` must hold the full password `Harbor Light #2024`, both in
the cluster and in what Helm manages (patching the Secret with kubectl is not enough).

mission.name: 256 Bytes Of RAM
mission.description:
The thumbnail workers (`image-resizer`) need a bit more memory, so someone set
`resources.limits.memory: 256` in `image-resizer/values.yaml`, meaning "256 megabytes". The release
fails to install and ends up `failed`:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: server-side apply failed for object helmissions/image-resizer
  apps/v1, Kind=Deployment: Deployment.apps "image-resizer" is invalid:
  spec.template.spec.containers[0].resources.requests: Invalid value: "128Mi":
  must be less than or equal to memory limit of 256
No worker pods exist.
mission.objective:
Release `image-resizer` in namespace `helmissions` is deployed with 2 ready pods and a memory
limit of 256Mi (a quarter of a gibibyte) coming from the Helm values, while the 128Mi request is
kept. Patching the Deployment with kubectl does not count.

mission.description:
The `upload-proxy` release is deployed with `maxUploadBytes: 1048576` (exactly 1 MiB) in
`values.yaml`, but the pod crash-loops: `proxy: MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES must be an integer number of bytes,
got '1.048576e+06'`. Looking at the ConfigMap, the number really was rewritten into scientific
notation. A colleague notes that other environments override the value in their own values
files, e.g. 5242880 for the media cluster.
mission.objective:
Release `upload-proxy` in namespace `helmissions` is deployed with its pod Ready and the ConfigMap
`upload-proxy-limits` holding `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES: "1048576"`. The chart itself must render plain
integers for any whole-number value, including 5242880 supplied through a values file.

mission.name: The Schema Says No
mission.description:
Release `search-api` will not install. The chart ships a `values.schema.json`, and Helm
validates the values against it before rendering anything:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: values don't meet the specifications of the schema(s) in the following chart(s):
  search-api:
  - at '/replicas': minimum: got 0, want 1
  - at '/logLevel': value must be one of 'debug', 'info', 'warn', 'error'
The platform team owns that schema (it is the contract with the log pipeline and the SLO
policy), and it must stay exactly as it is.
mission.objective:
Release `search-api` is deployed in namespace `helmissions` with its pods Ready, using a valid
`logLevel` and at least one replica. `search-api/values.schema.json` must be byte-for-byte unchanged,
and the release must not have been installed around the validation.

mission.name: 1.10 Became 1.1
mission.description:
The status page belongs to release train 1.10, and dashboards group pods by the label
`app.version`. After the last deploy (`./deploy.sh`) the pods are labelled `app.version=1.1`:
the 1.10 train and the (much older) 1.1 train now share a panel. `status-page/values.yaml`
says `appVersionLabel: 1.10`, and `helm get values status-page` shows `appVersionLabel: 1.1`.
mission.objective:
Release `status-page` in namespace `helmissions` is deployed with its pod Ready, and the Deployment
and its running pods carry the label `app.version` with the exact string value `1.10`
(not `1.1`). The change must come through Helm; relabelling pods with kubectl does not count.

mission.name: Unclosed Action
mission.description:
The editorial team's newsletter site, chart `pressroom`, has never made it to the cluster. After a
late-night edit to the homepage template the install now dies before anything is created:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: parse error at (pressroom/templates/configmap.yaml:13): unexpected "}" in operand
The chart lives in your workspace under `pressroom/`.
mission.objective:
Release `pressroom` is deployed in namespace `helmissions` from the chart in your workspace,
its pod is Ready, and the homepage served by the `pressroom` Service shows the site name taken
from `site.name` in the chart values (the name must follow the value, not be typed into the template).

mission.name: Mis-indented Resources
mission.description:
The platform team added CPU and memory limits to the `geoip` lookup service by passing the `resources`
block from values.yaml through `toYaml`. The deploy has not worked since:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: server-side apply failed for object helmissions/geoip-lookup apps/v1, Kind=Deployment:
  ... .spec.template.spec.containers[name="lookup"].limits: field not declared in schema
The chart is in your workspace under `geoip/`.
mission.objective:
Release `geoip` is deployed in namespace `helmissions`. The `lookup` container of Deployment
`geoip-lookup` carries the requests and limits defined in the chart's `resources` value (and follows
it when it is overridden), and its pod is Ready.

mission.name: Empty Image
mission.description:
The checkout team's `receipts` release was installed last night and has been "deploying" ever since.
`helm status receipts` says deployed, but the pods never start:
  receipts-api-...   0/1   InvalidImageName
`kubectl describe pod` complains about the image reference. The chart is in your workspace under `receipts/`.
mission.objective:
Release `receipts` in namespace `helmissions` is upgraded from the chart in your workspace (a new
revision), both `receipts-api` pods are Ready on the `nginx:1.27-alpine` image, and the chart builds its
image reference from the `image.repository` and `image.tag` values (overriding them must change the image).

mission.name: Lost In with
mission.description:
The platform team asked every chart to stamp pods with ownership labels and with the name of the release
that created them. After the change to the `tileserver` chart, the geo team can no longer deploy:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: tileserver/templates/deployment.yaml:18:51
    executing "tileserver/templates/deployment.yaml" at <.Release.Name>:
      nil pointer evaluating interface {}.Name
The chart is in your workspace under `tileserver/`.
mission.objective:
Release `tiles` is deployed in namespace `helmissions` from the chart in your workspace. Its pod is Ready
and carries the labels from the `podLabels` value plus a `tileserver.example.com/release` label whose
value is the name of the release (whatever the release is called).

mission.name: function "uppercase" not defined
mission.description:
The logistics team wants the `dispatch` worker to receive its environment name in capitals. Someone added
a pipe to the Deployment template and since then nothing installs:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: parse error at (dispatch/templates/deployment.yaml:28): function "uppercase" not defined
The chart is in your workspace under `dispatch/`.
mission.objective:
Release `dispatch` is deployed in namespace `helmissions` from the chart in your workspace. Its worker pod is
Ready and receives `APP_ENV=PRODUCTION`, derived from the `environment` value (changing the value, for example
to `staging`, must change the variable to `STAGING`).

mission.name: Default Always Wins
mission.description:
The release manager pinned `image.tag: v1.10` in the `echo-api` chart's values.yaml, but the `echo` release
keeps trying to run a different tag. Pods sit in ErrImagePull / ImagePullBackOff for
`traefik/whoami:v1.11-rc1`, an image that was never published, and `--set image.tag=...` seems to be ignored
too. The chart is in your workspace under `echo-api/`.
mission.objective:
Release `echo` in namespace `helmissions` is upgraded from the chart in your workspace (a new revision) and
both `echo` pods are Ready on the tag pinned in values.yaml. An explicitly set `image.tag` must win, and when
`image.tag` is empty the chart's appVersion must still be used as the fallback.

mission.name: no template named "shop.labels"
mission.description:
The shop chart was renamed to `storefront` last sprint and all helper definitions were renamed with it.
Now the release pipeline fails on every run:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: ... executing "storefront/templates/service.yaml" at <include "shop.labels" .>:
  error calling include: template: no template "shop.labels" associated with template "gotpl"
The chart is in your workspace under `storefront/`.
mission.objective:
Release `shop` is deployed in namespace `helmissions` from the `storefront` chart in your workspace. Its 2 pods
are Ready, and the Service carries the same standard labels (name, instance, version, managed-by) as the
Deployment, produced by the shared label helper.

mission.name: Misaligned Labels
mission.description:
The finance platform team's nightly `ledger-recon` chart was refactored to use a shared label helper.
Since the change the CronJob cannot be installed:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: YAML parse error on ledger-recon/templates/cronjob.yaml: error converting YAML to JSON:
  yaml: line 5: mapping values are not allowed in this context
The ConfigMap in the same chart, which uses the same helper, renders fine. The chart is in your workspace under
`ledger-recon/`.
mission.objective:
Release `reconcile` is deployed in namespace `helmissions` from the chart in your workspace. The CronJob
`reconcile` exists, is not suspended, and carries all three standard labels from the helper (name, instance,
component) in its metadata, exactly like the ConfigMap `reconcile-config`.

mission.name: Wrong Ingress API
mission.description:
The `docs-portal` chart supports old and new clusters by picking the Ingress apiVersion from the cluster's
capabilities. On our current cluster it picks the wrong one and the install is rejected:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: unable to build kubernetes objects from release manifest: resource mapping not found
  for name: "portal" namespace: "" from "": no matches for kind "Ingress" in version "networking.k8s.io/v1beta1"
The cluster certainly serves Ingress - `kubectl api-resources | grep ingresses` lists it. The chart is in your
workspace under `docs-portal/`.
mission.objective:
Release `portal` is deployed in namespace `helmissions` from the chart in your workspace, with the Ingress object
`portal` created under `networking.k8s.io/v1` (the chart's `ingress.enabled` stays true) and the Deployment's
pod Ready. Rendering the chart against this cluster's real API capabilities must produce the v1 Ingress.

mission.name: Duplicate Port Names
mission.description:
The `mesh-edge` chart drives its container ports and Service ports from one `ports` list in values.yaml.
Adding the admin and metrics entries last week broke the deploy:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: server-side apply failed for object helmissions/edge /v1, Kind=Service:
  Service "edge" is invalid: spec.ports[1].name: Duplicate value: "http"
The chart is in your workspace under `mesh-edge/`.
mission.objective:
Release `edge` is deployed in namespace `helmissions` from the chart in your workspace. Its Service exposes every
entry of the `ports` value (all three ports, each with its own unique name and the right port number), and the
pod is Ready and reachable through the Service.

mission.name: Number In An Env Var
mission.description:
The mail team made the relay's listen port configurable through `listenPort` in values.yaml and passed it to
the container as an environment variable. The release has not deployed since:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: server-side apply failed for object helmissions/relay apps/v1, Kind=Deployment:
  ... .env[name="WHOAMI_PORT_NUMBER"].value: expected string, got &value.valueUnstructured{Value:2525}
(Helm 3 words it as: json: cannot unmarshal number into Go struct field EnvVar.value of type string.)
The chart is in your workspace under `smtp-relay/`.
mission.objective:
Release `relay` is deployed in namespace `helmissions` from the chart in your workspace. The container gets the
environment variable `WHOAMI_PORT_NUMBER` with the value of `listenPort` (as a string), and changing `listenPort`
changes the variable. The pod is Ready and the `relay` Service has an endpoint.

mission.name: Literal Braces
mission.description:
The `orders` release (chart `orders-api`) is deployed, but the API pod never becomes Ready. Its readiness check
cannot connect to the database, and the logs say it is talking to a host with curly braces in its name:
  orders-api talking to {{ .Release.Name }}-db:5432
The chart's values.yaml defines the database host as `"{{ .Release.Name }}-db"` so that each release talks to its
own database Service. The chart is in your workspace under `orders-api/`.
mission.objective:
Release `orders` in namespace `helmissions` is upgraded from the chart in your workspace (a new revision). The API
pod is Ready and `DB_HOST` is the real service name `<release name>-db`, derived from the release name (rendering
the chart under another release name must give that release's own `<name>-db`).

mission.name: %!d(float64=8080)
mission.description:
The telemetry team's `ingest` release shows `deployed`, but its pod restarts in a loop (CrashLoopBackOff).
The container logs a flag-parsing complaint, and the startup arguments contain something that looks like
Go's formatting error:
  --port=%!d(float64=8080)
The chart is in your workspace under `ingest/`; the port comes from `port: 8080` in its values.
mission.objective:
Release `ingest` in namespace `helmissions` is upgraded from the chart in your workspace (a new revision). The
pod is Ready, starts with a valid `--port=<port>` argument built from the `port` value, and the `ingest` Service
has an endpoint. Any numeric port set in a values file must work, not only 8080.

mission.name: The Vanishing Config File
mission.description:
The `legacy-site` chart ships its nginx server block as `files/site.conf` and loads it into a ConfigMap with
`.Files.Get`. The release `site` installs without any error, but its pod never becomes Ready: the readiness probe
on /healthz keeps failing. `kubectl get configmap site-nginx -o yaml` shows a `default.conf` key with nothing in it,
although `files/site.conf` is right there in your workspace and is not empty. The chart is under `legacy-site/`.
mission.objective:
Release `site` in namespace `helmissions` is upgraded from the chart in your workspace (a new revision). The
nginx configuration delivered to the pod is the server block from the chart (listening on 8080 with a /healthz
location), the pod is Ready, and the `site` Service answers /healthz.

mission.name: illegal base64 data
mission.description:
The payments team added a Secret for the provider API key to the `payments-gw` chart and the release `gateway`
can no longer be installed:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: server-side apply failed for object helmissions/gateway-provider /v1, Kind=Secret:
  ... unable to convert unstructured object to /v1, Kind=Secret: error decoding from json: illegal base64 data at input byte 2
The sandbox key in the chart values is plain text, exactly as the provider issued it. The chart is in your workspace
under `payments-gw/`.
mission.objective:
Release `gateway` is deployed in namespace `helmissions` from the chart in your workspace. The Secret
`gateway-provider` exposes the key under `api-key`, and its decoded value is exactly the `provider.apiKey` value
(values.yaml keeps the key in plain text; overriding the value must change the Secret). The gateway pod is Ready.

mission.name: Helper Needs A Dict
mission.description:
The mail platform team moved naming and labels of the `mailer` chart's two components (the HTTP `api` and the queue
`worker`) into shared helpers. The helpers' comment says they take a dictionary; the templates that call them were
updated in a hurry and now nothing renders:
  Error: ... mailer/templates/worker.yaml:4:11 executing "mailer/templates/worker.yaml" at <include "mailer.fullname" .>:
  error calling include: ... executing "mailer.fullname" at <.ctx.Release.Name>: nil pointer evaluating interface {}.Release
The chart is in your workspace under `mailer/`.
mission.objective:
Release `mailer` is deployed in namespace `helmissions` from the chart in your workspace. It has two Deployments with
distinct names, `mailer-api` and `mailer-worker`, each labelled with its own `app.kubernetes.io/component`, both pods
are Ready, and the `mailer-api` Service routes to the api pod.

mission.name: Lines Glued Together
mission.description:
Someone "tidied up" the whitespace in the `thumbnailer` Deployment template. Since then the release can't be installed,
and the error mentions neither Kubernetes nor values:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: YAML parse error on thumbnailer/templates/deployment.yaml: error converting YAML to JSON:
  yaml: line 6: mapping values are not allowed in this context
The chart is in your workspace under `thumbnailer/`.
mission.objective:
Release `thumbs` is deployed in namespace `helmissions` from the chart in your workspace with 2 ready replicas.
The Deployment keeps all its settings (replicas from `replicaCount`, `revisionHistoryLimit: 2`) and the `thumbs`
Service has 2 ready endpoints.

mission.name: The Disappearing Deployment
mission.description:
The `status` release (chart `status-page`) installed without a single error and `helm status status` says
`deployed`. But the public status page is down: `kubectl get pods -n helmissions` shows nothing at all, while
a Service called `status` exists and points at nothing. The chart keeps its Deployment and Service together in
`templates/app.yaml`. The chart is in your workspace under `status-page/`.
mission.objective:
Release `status` in namespace `helmissions` is upgraded from the chart in your workspace (a new revision). The
release contains both a Deployment and a Service named `status`, 2 pods are Ready, and the Service has 2 ready
endpoints.

mission.name: No Endpoints
mission.description:
The `payments` release is up: `kubectl get pods` shows 2/2 Running and Ready, and `helm status payments` is deployed.
But nothing can reach the API. Calls to the `payments` Service time out, and
  kubectl get endpoints payments -n helmissions
lists no addresses at all. The chart labels pods through the shared helpers in `_helpers.tpl`. The chart is in your
workspace under `payments/`.
mission.objective:
Release `payments` in namespace `helmissions` is upgraded from the chart in your workspace (a new revision). The
Service `payments` has 2 ready endpoints, and the chart builds the Service selector from the same label helper that
builds the Deployment's selector, so they can never drift apart (rendering under another release name must keep them
identical and specific to that release).

mission.name: The Password Changes Every Deploy
mission.description:
The `ledgerdb` release generates its database password in the chart with `randAlphaNum`. Every `helm upgrade`
(even one that only changes the replica count) produces a new password, restarts the pod through the checksum
annotation, and locks out clients that still hold the old one. `helm history ledgerdb -n helmissions` already shows
two revisions. The fingerprint (sha256) of the password the billing system registered is stored in the ConfigMap
`registered-credentials` in the same namespace. The chart is in your workspace under `ledger-db/`.
mission.objective:
Release `ledgerdb` in namespace `helmissions` is upgraded from the fixed chart in your workspace. After the upgrade
the password in Secret `ledgerdb-credentials` is still the one whose fingerprint is stored in `registered-credentials`,
and a brand-new install of the chart followed by further upgrades keeps its generated password unchanged. The
database pod is Ready.

mission.name: Born Failed
mission.description:
The billing team's first deploy of `invoice-api` blew up and they have gone home.
The pipeline log ends with:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: server-side apply failed for object helmissions/invoice-api /v1, Kind=Service:
  Service "invoice-api" is invalid: spec.type: Unsupported value: "ClusterIp": supported values: ...
Re-running `helm install invoice-api ./invoice-api` now says the release name is still in use, and
`helm list` does not show it as a healthy release. The chart is in your workspace under `invoice-api/`.
mission.objective:
Release `invoice-api` in namespace `helmissions` is in the `deployed` state with its latest revision
built from the chart in your workspace, the Deployment `invoice-api` has 2 ready pods and the
Service `invoice-api` has ready endpoints.

mission.name: Fix Forward
mission.description:
`ledger-sync` 1.0 has been running happily. Today the team shipped chart 1.1, which switches the worker
to incremental reconciliation (`RECONCILE_MODE=incremental`, `BATCH_SIZE=500`) and scales it to 2 replicas.
The upgrade failed:
  Error: UPGRADE FAILED: server-side apply failed for object helmissions/ledger-sync apps/v1, Kind=Deployment:
  Deployment.apps "ledger-sync" is invalid: ... readinessProbe ... may not specify more than 1 handler type
`helm status` now reports the release as `failed`, and the old pod is still serving traffic.
The 1.1 chart is in your workspace under `ledger-sync/`.
mission.objective:
Release `ledger-sync` in namespace `helmissions` is `deployed` on a new revision created by an upgrade
(history keeps the failed revision), runs chart 1.1.0 with the incremental mode and batch size
settings live on the Deployment, and has 2 ready pods. A rollback to 1.0 does not count.

mission.name: Timed Out Waiting
mission.description:
The pipeline upgrades the documentation portal to chart 2.1 (2 replicas plus a readiness probe) with
`helm upgrade docs-portal ./docs-portal --wait --timeout 30s`. After half a minute it gives up:
  Error: UPGRADE FAILED: resource Deployment/helmissions/docs-portal not ready. status: InProgress,
  message: Updated: 1/2 ... context deadline exceeded
`helm status` says `failed`, and `kubectl get pods` shows the new pod running but `0/1` ready.
Nobody is sure whether to blame the cluster, the image or Helm. The chart is in `docs-portal/`.
mission.objective:
Release `docs-portal` in namespace `helmissions` is `deployed` after a successful `--wait` upgrade
(not a rollback), chart 2.1.0 is live with 2 ready replicas, and the container still has a readiness
probe configured.

mission.name: The Upgrade That Undid Itself
mission.description:
Last night's deploy of `telemetry-gw` 0.5 (3 replicas, `SAMPLE_RATE=0.25`, a 15-minute usage report)
ran with the atomic/rollback-on-failure flag. The pipeline went red, the gateway is still up on the old
settings, and nobody can tell what actually happened: `helm history` shows three revisions and the
release is `deployed` again. The pipeline output only said:
  Error: UPGRADE FAILED: release telemetry-gw failed, and has been rolled back due to ...
The 0.5 chart is in your workspace under `telemetry-gw/`.
mission.objective:
Release `telemetry-gw` in namespace `helmissions` is `deployed` on a newest revision that is a real
upgrade (not a rollback) running chart 0.5.0: 3 ready replicas, `SAMPLE_RATE=0.25` on the Deployment,
and the usage-report CronJob present with a valid schedule.

mission.name: First Deploy Breaks CI
mission.description:
The pipeline for the logistics portal's `shipment-tracker` has been green for months on the staging
environment, but the very first deploy to a brand-new environment fails in `ci/deploy.sh`:
  Deploying shipment-tracker to namespace helmissions
  Error: UPGRADE FAILED: "shipment-tracker" has no deployed releases
Nothing exists in the namespace yet. Whoever rolls this pipeline out to the next new environment will
hit the same wall. The chart and the script are in your workspace (`shipment-tracker/`, `ci/deploy.sh`).
mission.objective:
Running `bash ci/deploy.sh` from the workspace deploys release `shipment-tracker` into namespace
`helmissions` (status `deployed`, pod Ready), and the same script also succeeds, twice in a row, in a
fresh namespace `helmissions-ci` that has no release yet.

mission.name: Invalid Ownership Metadata
mission.description:
An engineer created the ConfigMap `desk-settings` by hand last year (`kubectl create configmap`) to tune the
ticket desk. The new `support-desk` chart now manages that same ConfigMap, and the first install fails:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: unable to continue with install: ConfigMap "desk-settings" in namespace
  "helmissions" exists and cannot be imported into the current release: invalid ownership metadata; ...
Nothing was created. The chart is in your workspace under `support-desk/`; the chart's settings are the
ones the team wants in production, not the hand-made ones.
mission.objective:
Release `support-desk` is `deployed` in namespace `helmissions`. The ConfigMap `desk-settings` is part of
the release (Helm ownership metadata for `support-desk`) and every key the chart defines carries the chart's
value (MAX_OPEN_TICKETS=200, SLA_HOURS=8). The Deployment `support-desk` has a Ready pod.

mission.name: Field Is Immutable
mission.description:
Release 1.1 of the `catalog-search` chart only "tidies up the labels" to the recommended
`app.kubernetes.io/*` set. The upgrade of the running 1.0 release fails:
  Error: UPGRADE FAILED: server-side apply failed for object helmissions/catalog-search apps/v1,
  Kind=Deployment: Deployment.apps "catalog-search" is invalid: spec.selector: Invalid value: ...: field is immutable
`helm status` shows `failed`, the 1.0 pods keep serving. The 1.1 chart is in your workspace under
`catalog-search/`. Search must not go down and the release history must survive.
mission.objective:
Release `catalog-search` in namespace `helmissions` is `deployed` on chart 1.1.0 through an upgrade
(revision 1 is still in `helm history`), the Deployment's selector is still the one 1.0 created
(`app: catalog-search`), the running pods also carry the new `app.kubernetes.io/name=catalog-search`
label, 2 pods are Ready and the Service has endpoints.

mission.name: Bring Back Revision 2's Setting
mission.description:
Customers report that product search returns nothing since "last Tuesday". The shop's `product-search`
release has been upgraded five times by three different people, always "just a quick config tweak".
`helm history product-search -n helmissions` lists five revisions that all say `Upgrade complete`.
Somebody remembers that search was working after the second revision, and that later revisions
contain changes the team still wants. The chart (unchanged by those tweaks) is in your workspace
under `product-search/`.
mission.objective:
Release `product-search` in namespace `helmissions` is `deployed` on a NEW revision created by an upgrade
(not a rollback) in which `FEATURE_SEARCH` is `true` again, while the wanted later tweaks are still live:
`CACHE_TTL_SECONDS=600`, `LOG_LEVEL=warn`, 2 replicas and `FEATURE_RECOMMEND=false`.

mission.name: The Kept Secret
mission.description:
The shop was renamed: release `shop` was uninstalled and the new chart `storefront` should replace it.
The database Secret `db-credentials` was deliberately left in place (it carries `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep`
so nobody loses credentials by accident), and the new chart ships a Secret with the same name.
Installing the new release fails:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: unable to continue with install: Secret "db-credentials" in namespace "helmissions"
  exists and cannot be imported into the current release: invalid ownership metadata; annotation validation error:
  key "meta.helm.sh/release-name" must equal "storefront": current value is "shop"
The `storefront` chart is in your workspace.
mission.objective:
Release `storefront` is `deployed` in namespace `helmissions` and its pod is Ready. The Secret
`db-credentials` exists and belongs to release `storefront` (it appears in the release manifest and its Helm
ownership annotations name `storefront`). No release `shop` exists.

mission.name: Undo An Uninstall
mission.description:
Before a maintenance window someone ran `helm uninstall loyalty-points -n helmissions --keep-history` to free the
namespace "for a minute". The window is over, the pods are gone and the loyalty page is down.
`helm list -n helmissions` shows nothing, although `helm list --uninstalled` knows the release. The chart
directory is not available on this machine, and nobody remembers the exact values the last deploy used.
mission.objective:
Release `loyalty-points` in namespace `helmissions` is `deployed` again with its history continued (the old
revisions are still listed and the newest revision is a rollback), running exactly the configuration it had when it
was uninstalled: chart 1.1.0, 2 ready replicas and `TIER_GOLD_THRESHOLD=500`.

mission.name: Must Be No More Than 63 Characters
mission.description:
Platform naming rules require the release name `customer-notification-dispatcher-production-eu` for the EU
production environment. Every other environment (short release names) deploys fine, but this one does not:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: ... Service "customer-notification-dispatcher-production-eu-notification-dispatcher"
  is invalid: metadata.name: Invalid value: "...": must be no more than 63 characters
The release name itself cannot be changed. The chart is in your workspace under `notification-dispatcher/`.
mission.objective:
Release `customer-notification-dispatcher-production-eu` (exactly that name) is `deployed` in namespace
`helmissions`, every Service it owns has a valid name (at most 63 characters) and its Deployment has a Ready pod.

mission.name: Another Operation In Progress
mission.description:
The CI runner was OOM-killed halfway through the `warehouse-stock` 1.1 deploy. Every pipeline run since then
fails immediately:
  Error: UPGRADE FAILED: another operation (install/upgrade/rollback) is in progress
Nobody is running Helm at the moment. `helm list -n helmissions` shows the release as `pending-upgrade`,
and `helm history` shows a revision whose description is stuck at "Preparing upgrade". The 1.1 chart that the
pipeline was deploying is in your workspace under `warehouse-stock/`.
mission.objective:
Release `warehouse-stock` in namespace `helmissions` is `deployed` (not pending) on chart 1.1.0 from your
workspace: 2 ready replicas with `SYNC_INTERVAL_SECONDS=30`, and the newest revision is not the interrupted one.

mission.name: No Matches For Kind
mission.description:
The platform team packaged a small operator-less "backup scheduler": a CustomResourceDefinition
(`BackupSchedule`), one `BackupSchedule` resource named `nightly` and a controller Deployment, all in the chart
`backup-scheduler`. On a clean cluster the install fails before anything is created:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: unable to build kubernetes objects from release manifest: resource mapping not
  found for name: "nightly" namespace: "" from "": no matches for kind "BackupSchedule" in version
  "helmissions.io/v1"
  ensure CRDs are installed first
The chart is in your workspace under `backup-scheduler/`.
mission.objective:
Release `backup-scheduler` is `deployed` in namespace `helmissions`; the CRD `backupschedules.helmissions.io`
exists in the cluster, the `BackupSchedule` named `nightly` exists and is part of the release, and the controller
Deployment is Ready.

mission.name: Red Test Suite
mission.description:
The `rating-service` release is live and answers requests, but the release's smoke test is red. The post-deploy
job runs `helm test rating-service -n helmissions` and fails every time:
  Error: 1 error occurred:
      * pod rating-service-test-connection failed
Developers have started ignoring the failure because "the service works". The chart, including its
test pod, is in your workspace under `rating-service/`.
mission.objective:
A `helm test rating-service -n helmissions` run succeeds against the live release (the test hook is still
defined and still exercises the Service), and the release is `deployed` with 1 ready pod.
concepts: hooks are stored in the release

mission.name: Broken NOTES.txt
mission.description:
A trivial chart, `status-page`, refuses to install even though the Deployment and Service templates look fine.
The error points at a file that is not even a Kubernetes manifest:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: template: status-page/templates/NOTES.txt:4:23: executing
  "status-page/templates/NOTES.txt" at <.Values.ingress.host>: nil pointer evaluating interface {}.host
Nothing is created in the cluster. The chart is in your workspace under `status-page/`.
mission.objective:
Release `status-page` is `deployed` in namespace `helmissions` with a Ready pod, and `helm get notes status-page`
prints the post-install notes including an `http://` URL for the page.

mission.name: Roll It Back
mission.description:
The marketing site's quote widget is blank. `quotes-api` was upgraded an hour ago and nobody has
looked at it since: `helm list -n helmissions` says `deployed`, yet `kubectl get pods -n helmissions`
shows the pod stuck in `ErrImagePull` / `ImagePullBackOff` and the Service has no endpoints.
The chart source lives in another team's repository - you only have cluster access.
mission.objective:
Release `quotes-api` in namespace `helmissions` serves traffic again with a Ready pod running the image
that was in production before the bad upgrade, and the release history shows the recovery as a
rollback record (not a brand-new upgrade).

mission.name: The Hotfix That Vanished
mission.description:
Yesterday `order-sync` ran out of database connections and the on-call engineer fixed it live with
`kubectl set env deployment/order-sync DB_POOL_SIZE=40`. This morning the pipeline shipped an unrelated
log-level change (`ci/deploy.sh`) and the same outage is back: the service page says
`status=degraded - connection pool exhausted`. Nobody touched the pool size in Git.
The chart and the pipeline's values live in your workspace.
mission.objective:
Release `order-sync` in namespace `helmissions` is deployed from the workspace chart with
`DB_POOL_SIZE=40` in the live pods, the service reports `status=ok`, and the setting comes from the
chart/values files the pipeline deploys with - so the next run of `ci/deploy.sh` keeps it.

mission.name: Find The Last Good Revision
mission.description:
`freight-quote` had a rough week: six deploys, three different people, no changelog. Carriers are now
complaining that every shipment is quoted at a rate of 0, and the integration team says insurance
quotes were working on Wednesday. `helm history freight-quote -n helmissions` shows a tidy column of
`superseded` revisions and one `deployed` one - Helm can't tell you which of them was healthy.
Only the cluster remembers: the chart source is not available to you.
mission.objective:
Release `freight-quote` in namespace `helmissions` is deployed with all pods Ready, and
`GET /quote` on the Service answers with `"rate":42` and `"insurance":true`. The newest revision must
be the rollback to the newest revision that behaved correctly.

mission.name: Somebody Deleted The Service
mission.description:
Order notifications stopped at 09:40. The `order-service` logs are full of
`dial tcp: lookup sms-gateway.helmissions.svc: no such host`. The `sms-gateway` pods are Running and
Ready, `helm list -n helmissions` still shows the release as `deployed` - but
`kubectl get svc -n helmissions` is empty. Someone ran a "cleanup" with `kubectl delete` this morning.
The chart is in your workspace under `sms-gateway/`.
mission.objective:
Service `sms-gateway` exists again in namespace `helmissions`, is owned by the Helm release
`sms-gateway` (Helm ownership metadata present), has ready endpoints and answers HTTP requests.
Helm must have recorded the recovery as a new revision.

mission.name: Rolled Back But Still Broken
mission.description:
Someone pushed `rateLimit: 1` to `edge-throttle` and the API started rejecting almost every request.
They noticed, restarted the pods to "make sure", and then ran `helm rollback edge-throttle 1`. Helm says
`Rollback was a success`, `kubectl get configmap edge-throttle-config -o yaml` shows `RATE_LIMIT: "100"`,
yet the service still answers `rate_limit=1` and customers are still being throttled.
The chart is in your workspace under `edge-throttle/`.
mission.objective:
Release `edge-throttle` in namespace `helmissions` is deployed from the workspace chart and the running
pods answer `rate_limit=100`. The chart itself must make pods restart whenever its configuration
changes, so the next config change or rollback cannot leave pods on stale settings.

mission.name: The Good Revision Is Gone
mission.description:
`geo-lookup` answers every request with `503 {"error":"provider maps-v1-eu is retired"}`. Last week it
worked. The obvious move is `helm rollback geo-lookup 1`, but `helm history geo-lookup -n helmissions`
starts at revision 2 and the rollback fails because the revision does not exist. The pipeline's
`ci/deploy.sh` deploys with `--history-max 3`. The chart and the pipeline's values file are in your
workspace.
mission.objective:
Release `geo-lookup` in namespace `helmissions` is deployed from the workspace chart and `GET /lookup`
answers `200` with `"provider":"maps-v2"`, `"ttl":300` and `"trace":false`. The values the pipeline deploys
with (`values-prod.yaml` + chart defaults) must render that same configuration.

mission.name: Immutable Job Template
mission.description:
The `catalog` 1.1.0 release ships a new seed dataset, so the chart bumps the seed Job's `SEED_VERSION`
from 1 to 2. The upgrade fails every time:
  UPGRADE FAILED: ... Job.batch "catalog-seed" is invalid: spec.template: Invalid value: ... field is immutable
`helm history catalog -n helmissions` shows revision 2 as `failed`, and the API is still serving the old
catalog. The chart is in your workspace under `catalog-seed/`.
mission.objective:
Release `catalog` in namespace `helmissions` is `deployed` from the 1.1.0 chart, the seed Job that is live
in the cluster runs with `SEED_VERSION=2` and has completed successfully, and the API is Ready.

mission.name: The Invisible Release
mission.description:
`audit-gateway` has been down since the 08:12 deploy: the pod is in `CrashLoopBackOff`. The pipeline log
(`ci/deploy.log` in your workspace) says `Release "audit-gateway" has been upgraded`, revision 2 -
but on your terminal `helm list -n helmissions` prints nothing and
`helm history audit-gateway -n helmissions` says the release is not found. The Deployment is clearly
there and carries Helm's ownership labels.
mission.objective:
The Helm release `audit-gateway` that the pipeline manages (the one with the history the deploy log
talks about) is `deployed` with a newest revision that is a rollback to its first revision, and the
gateway pod is Ready. Do not create a second release.

mission.name: The CRD That Never Updated
mission.description:
Chart `snapshot-scheduler` 2.0.0 adds a `retentionDays` field to the `SnapshotPolicy` CRD (it lives in the
chart's `crds/` folder) and the `nightly` policy in `templates/` now sets `retentionDays: 30`.
The upgrade from 1.0.0 fails:
  UPGRADE FAILED: server-side apply failed for object helmissions/nightly helmissions.io/v1, Kind=SnapshotPolicy:
  ... .spec.retentionDays: field not declared in schema
The CRD in your workspace clearly declares the field. The chart is under `snapshot-scheduler/`.
mission.objective:
Release `snapshots` in namespace `helmissions` is `deployed` from chart snapshot-scheduler 2.0.0, the
cluster's `snapshotpolicies.helmissions.io` CRD declares `retentionDays`, and the live `nightly`
SnapshotPolicy has `retentionDays: 30`.

mission.name: Pre-rollback Hook Says No
mission.description:
Revision 2 of `settlement-batch` is crash-looping (the Deployment cannot pull its image) and the nightly
settlement window opens in an hour. Your colleague already tried `helm rollback settlement-batch 1 -n helmissions`;

mission.name: Immutable ConfigMap

mission.name: Every Deploy Scales To 2

mission.name: Incident: Checkout Is Down

mission.name: Storefront Without Its Cache

`storefront-session-cache` both have a Ready pod. `storefront/Chart.yaml` must still declare the
`session-cache` dependency.

mission.name: Chart.lock Out Of Sync
mission.description:
`ledger` is released through a pipeline that starts with `helm dependency build ./ledger`. Since the
platform team shipped `ledger-db` 0.4.0 and `ledger/Chart.yaml` was bumped to require it, the pipeline stops at

with the WAL retention requested in `ledger/values.yaml`.

mission.name: No Matching Version
mission.description:
The search team wants to ship `searchdesk`, which caches results in `redis-lite` from the platform team's chart

mission.name: Same Chart Twice
mission.description:
The inventory API must talk to a read-write key-value store and a read-only replica, so the team listed the `kvstore`
subchart twice in `inventory/Chart.yaml` and wrote one settings block per instance in `values.yaml`. Nothing

Both the `inventory` chart and the `kvstore` chart are in your workspace.

mission.name: Values Not Reaching The Subchart
mission.description:
The photo desk asked for a beefier image resizer for election night: 3 replicas, photos capped at 800 px and JPEG

mission.name: One Setting For All Subcharts
mission.description:
The telemetry stack (gateway, `collector`, `exporter`) is supposed to stamp every span and metric with the region

mission.name: Disabled But Still Deployed

mission.name: Toggle A Group
mission.description:
The trading desk's developer sandbox must not run the monitoring stack (`metrics-agent`, `log-shipper`,

mission.name: No Repository Definition

The status page chart pulls `uptime-probe` from the platform team's "stable" repository using the short form

mission.name: Parent Needs Child's Value

mission.name: The Competing Dependency List
mission.description:

mission.name: A Subchart's Hook Blocks Everything
mission.description:

Release `ledger-api` in namespace `helmissions` is `deployed` with 1 ready pod, and the pre-install migration

mission.description:

Yet the init Job is part of the chart, nothing was deleted, and it works when run on its own. The hooks involved are the

Release `orders` in namespace `helmissions` is `deployed` with 1 ready pod, and both database hooks completed. A brand-new
install of the chart into an empty namespace also succeeds: the schema is always initialised first and migrated second,
proven by the state ConfigMap that the Jobs write (`initialized-at` before `migrated-at`).

mission.name: The Migration Ran Too Late
mission.description:

The new pod never gets past its init container (`Init:Error` / `Init:CrashLoopBackOff`), which logs

mission.objective:
Release `shipments` in namespace `helmissions` is `deployed` on chart 1.1.0 with all pods ready on the new version, and the
schema migration ran as part of the deploy. Upgrading a fresh 1.0.0 release to the workspace chart with `--wait` succeeds

mission.name: Uninstall Leaves A Mess
mission.description:

Uninstalling a release of the `export-batch` chart removes the scratch volume it created: after a full install and

mission.name: The Config That Hooked Itself Away
mission.description:
`helm install gateway ./route-gateway` reports success and `helm list` shows the release as `deployed`, yet the gateway never

The routing table ConfigMap is clearly defined in the chart, but `kubectl get configmap -n helmissions` does not list it, and

mission.objective:
Release `gateway` in namespace `helmissions` is `deployed` with 1 ready pod that serves the routing table (the response of

mission.name: "No Tests Found"
mission.description:
The `inventory-search` release has a test pod in its chart (`templates/tests/search-test.yaml`), and the pipeline's

Release `inventory-search` is installed as `search` in namespace `helmissions` and is `deployed` with 1 ready pod. `helm test search -n helmissions`
now actually runs the chart's test pod against the live search endpoint and succeeds (the test pod is a real hook of the release and the

concepts: hooks are stored in the release

mission.name: Forbidden Inside The Hook
mission.description:
The first install of `tenants` (chart `tenant-onboarding`) fails in its pre-install phase. The chart's pre-flight Job asks the

Helm reports `failed pre-install: resource Job/helmissions/tenants-preflight not ready`. The chart is in your workspace under `tenant-onboarding/`.
mission.objective:
Release `tenants` in namespace `helmissions` is `deployed` with 1 ready pod, and its pre-install preflight Job completed
successfully using permissions that the chart itself provides. A brand-new install of the chart into an empty namespace succeeds too,
without anyone creating RBAC objects by hand.

mission.name: The Secret Isn't There Yet
mission.description:
The first install of `payroll` hangs until the CI timeout (40s) and then fails:

The bootstrap Job's pod never starts: `kubectl describe pod` shows `Error: secret "payroll-db" not found`

The chart is in your workspace under `payroll-api/`.
mission.objective:
Release `payroll` in namespace `helmissions` is `deployed` with 1 ready pod, the pre-install bootstrap Job completed successfully
using the `payroll-db` Secret, and the Secret still exists afterwards for the application pod to use. A brand-new install of the chart

mission.name: Password In Git

Security wants it out of git and out of the Helm release, and the exposed password must be treated as compromised.

Release `ledger-api` in namespace `helmissions` is `deployed` and its pod is Ready. No file in your workspace
contains a plaintext password, the release's user-supplied values contain no password, and the pod's
`DB_PASSWORD` comes from a Kubernetes Secret reference. That Secret exists in the namespace, is not managed
by the Helm release, and holds a new password (not the leaked `Tr0ub4dor&3-ledger-prod`).

mission.name: 403 From The API

the pod never turns Ready and its log keeps repeating:

The API server answers `configmaps is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:helmissions:flag-sync" cannot
list resource "configmaps" in API group "" in the namespace "helmissions"`. The security team will review the
RBAC in this chart line by line.

Release `flag-sync` in namespace `helmissions` is deployed with a Ready pod whose log reports HTTP 200 for both
calls. The `flag-sync` ServiceAccount can read pods and ConfigMaps in its own namespace, but nothing more: no
wildcards in any rule, no write access, no access to Secrets or other namespaces, and no cluster-wide grants.

mission.name: Policy Blocks The Frontend
mission.description:

rule that is meant to let the web tier call the catalog backend. Since the rollout the frontend pod
never becomes Ready and its log says:

The catalog backend itself is Running and its Service has endpoints — a one-off pod can't reach it either,
which is expected. The security team insists the zero-trust posture stays.
mission.objective:
Release `shopfront` in namespace `helmissions` is deployed with the frontend pod Ready (it can reach the
catalog backend Service). The backend must remain protected: a pod that is not part of the web tier still
cannot connect to it, and the NetworkPolicies stay part of the release.

mission.name: Root Is Not Welcome
mission.description:
The platform baseline says every pod must set `runAsNonRoot: true`, and the `status-page` chart already does.
Since it was deployed, both replicas are stuck:
  kubectl get pods   ->   STATUS: CreateContainerConfigError
  Error: container has runAsNonRoot and image will run as root (pod: "status-page-...", container web)
The Deployment exists, the Service has no endpoints, and the public status page is down.
mission.objective:
Release `status-page` in namespace `helmissions` is deployed with 2 Ready pods behind its Service, which
answers HTTP. Every container still runs with `runAsNonRoot: true` and the processes inside really run as a
non-zero UID.

mission.name: Unauthorized Pull
mission.description:
The partner portal image lives in the company's private registry at `localhost:5002`. The release installs,
but its pods never start:
  STATUS: ImagePullBackOff
  Failed to pull image "localhost:5002/m8-portal/portal:1.0": ... pull access denied, repository does not exist

The image is there — `DEPLOY-TICKET.txt` in your workspace has the read-only pull account for the registry.

Release `portal` in namespace `helmissions` is deployed with 2 Ready pods that still pull
`localhost:5002/m8-portal/portal:1.0` from the private registry (which must keep requiring authentication).
The pods authenticate through a `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` Secret for `localhost:5002` holding working

mission.name: The Policy Gate
mission.description:
Every chart change must pass the company's CI policy gate before it may be deployed. The new `report-worker`
chart fails it:
  $ bash ci/policy.sh
  POLICY VIOLATION: gate/worker: image nginx:latest uses a floating tag (pin a version)
  POLICY VIOLATION: gate/worker: resources.limits.cpu and resources.limits.memory are required

The gate script belongs to the security team. The chart has not been deployed yet.

`bash ci/policy.sh` exits 0 for the chart in your workspace (without any change to the gate script itself), and
release `report-worker` is deployed in namespace `helmissions` from that chart with its pod Ready. The live
release satisfies the same rules: pinned image tags, cpu and memory limits on every container, readiness and
liveness probes on every container.

mission.name: Removed APIs
mission.description:
The Kubernetes platform team upgraded the cluster to v1.37 over the weekend. The `inventory-service` chart,
which deployed fine on the old cluster, now refuses to install:
  Error: unable to build kubernetes objects from release manifest: [resource mapping not found for name:
  "inventory" namespace: "" from "": no matches for kind "PodDisruptionBudget" in version "policy/v1beta1"
