  "autoscaling/v2beta2" ...]
Nothing was created and no CRDs are involved. The autoscaling and the disruption budget are both required
for production.
mission.objective:
Release `inventory` in namespace `helmissions` is deployed from the chart in your workspace with 2 Ready pods.
Both the PodDisruptionBudget (min available 1) and the HorizontalPodAutoscaler (2 to 4 replicas, 70% CPU)
exist in the cluster, created from API versions the cluster actually serves.

mission.name: Quota Says No
mission.description:
The `helmissions` namespace carries a ResourceQuota called `search-team-quota`. `helm install` of the
`search-indexer` chart reports success, but the Deployment never gets its pods:
  kubectl get deploy search-indexer   ->   READY 0/2
  kubectl get events   ->   Error creating: pods "search-indexer-..." is forbidden: failed quota:
  search-team-quota: must specify limits.cpu for: indexer; limits.memory for: indexer; requests.cpu for:
  indexer; requests.memory for: indexer
The quota is set by the platform team and is not negotiable.
mission.objective:
Release `search-indexer` in namespace `helmissions` has 2 Ready pods. The ResourceQuota `search-team-quota`
still exists with exactly its original limits, and every container of the release declares cpu and memory
requests and limits.

mission.name: Restricted Pod Security
mission.description:
The security team labelled the `helmissions` namespace with Pod Security Admission level `restricted`
(`pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted`). The `audit-gateway` release is `deployed`, but its
Deployment has no pods. The ReplicaSet events read:
  Error creating: pods "audit-gateway-..." is forbidden: violates PodSecurity "restricted:latest":
  allowPrivilegeEscalation != false (...), unrestricted capabilities (...), runAsNonRoot != true (...),
  seccompProfile (pod or containers ... must set securityContext.seccompProfile.type to "RuntimeDefault" or "Localhost")
The namespace policy is not up for debate.
mission.objective:
Release `audit-gateway` in namespace `helmissions` has a Ready pod, and the namespace still enforces the
`restricted` Pod Security level. Every container of the pod, init containers included, runs without privilege
escalation, with all Linux capabilities dropped, as non-root, under the RuntimeDefault seccomp profile.

mission.name: Verify Before You Trust
mission.description:
Policy PCI-7 says the payments gateway may only be deployed from a chart signed with the release key. The deploy
script already asks Helm to verify, and it stops the pipeline:
  $ ./deploy.sh
  Error: could not load provenance file dist/payments-gateway-1.0.0.tgz.prov: stat ...: no such file or directory
Nothing is installed. The signing key pair is in `keys/` (the secret key has no passphrase). Skipping
verification is not an option: the release has to be provably the artifact that the key holder signed.
mission.objective:
A packaged `payments-gateway` 1.0.0 chart and its `.prov` provenance file exist in your workspace (`dist/`), and
`helm verify` accepts them with the trusted release key. Release `payments-gateway` in namespace `helmissions` is
deployed from that signed package (deployed after it was signed) and its 2 pods are Ready.

mission.name: DRY With A Library
mission.description:
The ledger platform ships two charts, `ledger-api` and `ledger-worker`, and each one carries its own copy
of the label helper in `templates/_helpers.tpl`. The copies drifted: the api forgot the `part-of` label,
the worker spells it `ledger-platform`, only one of them records the chart name, and the dashboards that
group workloads by label now show them as unrelated systems.
The label standard is written down in `README.txt` in your workspace. Both releases are already
installed with the drifted labels.
mission.objective:
Both charts take their labels from one shared Helm library chart that lives in the workspace
(its Chart.yaml has `type: library`) and is declared as a dependency of `ledger-api` and `ledger-worker`.
Every object both charts render (and every pod template) carries exactly the label keys listed in
`README.txt`, with `part-of: ledger`. Releases `ledger-api` and `ledger-worker` in namespace `helmissions`
are upgraded (revision 2 or later), deployed, with Ready pods and the standard labels on the live
Deployments. Pod selectors must keep working, so the upgrade must not fail.

mission.name: Not A Library After All
mission.description:
The messaging team shares broker settings through a chart called `mqlib`, consumed by the
`invoice-mailer` and `receipt-mailer` charts. `invoice-mailer` installed fine, but installing
`receipt-mailer` in the same namespace now dies with:
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: Unable to continue with install: ConfigMap "mq-defaults" in namespace
  "helmissions" exists and cannot be imported into the current release: invalid ownership metadata;
  annotation validation error: key "meta.helm.sh/release-name" must equal "receipt-mailer": current value is "invoice-mailer"
Nobody wrote a ConfigMap called `mq-defaults` in either consumer chart. Both charts are in your workspace.
mission.objective:
`mqlib` is a proper Helm library chart: it declares `type: library`, helm refuses to install it on its own,
and it contributes no objects to the releases that use it. Releases `invoice-mailer` and `receipt-mailer` in
namespace `helmissions` are both `deployed` (invoice-mailer upgraded to revision 2 or later), each with
its own `<release>-mq` ConfigMap holding the broker address from its values.yaml, Ready pods, and no
`mq-defaults` ConfigMap anywhere in the namespace or in either release.

mission.name: Ship Via OCI
mission.description:
Payments publishes `payments-gateway` as an OCI chart in the internal registry (plain HTTP, so every
helm call needs `--plain-http`). Release 0.2.0 went out last week. Today the release job packaged 0.3.0 and
`./release.sh` printed `Pushed: ...` without complaint, yet the rollout step fails:
  Error: UPGRADE FAILED: failed to perform "FetchReference" on source: localhost:5001/.../charts/payments-gateway:0.3.0: not found
The registry is up and 0.2.0 still pulls fine. `release.sh`, `deploy.sh` and the chart are in your workspace;
`README.txt` has the registry convention.
mission.objective:
Chart `payments-gateway` 0.3.0 from the workspace is published at the platform's registry reference (the
`oci://` location in `README.txt` and `deploy.sh`, tag 0.3.0) with exactly the content of the workspace chart,
and release `payments-gateway` in namespace `helmissions` is upgraded to chart 0.3.0 from that reference:
deployed, revision 2 or later, 2 Ready pods.

mission.name: Patch After Render
mission.description:
FinOps now requires the label `cost-center: edge-platform` on every Kubernetes object the edge team deploys, and
security wants a `log-shipper` sidecar next to the gateway container. `edge-gateway` is a vendored upstream
chart: it has no values for either, and the policy is that vendored charts are never edited by hand.
A teammate started a Helm post-renderer plugin, `hm-cost-labeler` (it runs `kubectl kustomize`), but upgrading with it fails:
  Error: error while running post render on files: failed to invoke post-renderer plugin "hm-cost-labeler": plugin "hm-cost-labeler" exited with error
Release `edge-gateway` is running without the label and the sidecar. Chart and plugin sources are in your workspace.
mission.objective:
The chart in `edge-gateway/` is left untouched. Release `edge-gateway` in namespace `helmissions` is upgraded
(revision 2 or later) so that its stored manifest — what `helm get manifest` shows — has the label
`cost-center: edge-platform` on every object and on the pod template, and the Deployment runs a second container
named `log-shipper`. Pod selectors are unchanged. The release is `deployed` with 2 Ready pods (both containers ready),
and an installed post-renderer plugin produces the same result when rendering the chart with `helm template`.

mission.name: Plugin Won't Load
mission.description:
The SRE team wrote a small Helm plugin, `hm-audit`, that lists containers running without resource limits in a
release. It lives in `hm-audit/` in your workspace and the README says to install it with
`helm plugin install ./hm-audit`. On this machine that ends with an error like
  Error: fork/exec .../plugins/hm-audit/hooks/install-rules.sh: no such file or directory
and trying the command afterwards is no better:
  Error: fork/exec .../plugins/hm-audit/bin/audit.sh: no such file or directory
Release `checkout` is deployed in namespace `helmissions` and is the first thing the team wants audited.
mission.objective:
Plugin `hm-audit` is installed (`helm plugin list` shows it as a `cli/v1` plugin) and
`helm hm-audit checkout -n helmissions` runs successfully, reporting `containers=2 missing_limits=1` and naming
the container without limits. The plugin directory also installs cleanly from scratch, with its install hook
succeeding, so a colleague who runs `helm plugin install ./hm-audit` gets a working plugin.

mission.name: Kustomize Inflates Helm
mission.description:
The storefront team deploys the catalog API through a GitOps folder: `platform/kustomization.yaml` inflates the
vendored `catalog-api` chart with a `helmCharts` entry and then adds an `env: prod` label with a kustomize
transformer. Nobody has built this folder on a fresh checkout before. `kubectl kustomize --enable-helm platform` stops with:
  error: no repo specified for pull, no chart found at ''
The chart sits in `platform/charts/catalog-api/` and the prod values in `platform/values/prod.yaml`;
`README.txt` shows how the folder is meant to be deployed (kustomize renders, kubectl applies, no Helm release).
mission.objective:
`kubectl kustomize --enable-helm platform` renders the `catalog-api` chart with the prod values, straight from
the `helmCharts` entry of `platform/kustomization.yaml` (it must stay a kustomize-inflated chart, not pasted YAML),
including the `env: prod` label on the objects and the pod template. The result is applied: in namespace
`helmissions` a Deployment `catalog-api` runs 2 Ready pods with `CACHE_TTL_SECONDS=600` and the `env=prod` label,
with a Service `catalog-api` in front. No Helm release is involved.

mission.name: Stale Index
mission.description:
The harbour team publishes `tide-tracker` through a classic chart repository that is just a folder served over HTTP
(workspace link `repo/`, served at the URL in `README.txt`, added on this machine as `hm-tides`). The release job copied
`tide-tracker-1.3.0.tgz` into the folder this morning and went home. Operators try to roll it out:
  Error: UPGRADE FAILED: chart "tide-tracker" matching 1.3.0 not found in hm-tides index. (try 'helm repo update'). no chart version found for tide-tracker-1.3.0
Running `helm repo update` changes nothing. Version 1.2.0 is deployed as release `tide-tracker`; an older 1.1.0
is still pinned by a regional cluster and must keep being downloadable from the same repository.
mission.objective:
The repository index that is served at the repository URL lists `tide-tracker` versions 1.1.0, 1.2.0 and 1.3.0,
each with a digest that matches its tarball, and every listed version can be downloaded (`helm pull hm-tides/tide-tracker
--version X`). Release `tide-tracker` in namespace `helmissions` is upgraded from the `hm-tides` repository to chart 1.3.0
(forecast window of 48 hours running in its pod). `index.yaml` is produced by Helm, not typed by hand.

mission.name: Catch Typos With A Schema
mission.description:
Last night's order backlog was blamed on the `queue-worker` chart: prod was supposed to run 3 workers that are probed every 5
seconds, but `kubectl get deploy` shows a single replica probed every 2 seconds. Helm raised no error at all, because the
production override file `values-prod.yaml` contains misspelled keys and Helm treats unknown values as perfectly
fine. The incident review wants the chart to refuse values it does not know about. The chart is `queue-worker/`
in your workspace, `values-prod.yaml` sits next to it, and the release `queue-worker` is deployed with that file.
mission.objective:
The chart has a `values.schema.json` that rejects unknown keys at every level of the documented values
(top level, `image`, `resources`, `probes.readiness`, ...) and wrong types (`replicaCount` must be an integer), while still accepting every documented
value and the free-form `extraEnv` / `podAnnotations` maps. Rendering with a typo'd key (for example `--set replicaCnt=3`) fails;
rendering the chart with its defaults works. `values-prod.yaml` passes the schema and release `queue-worker` in namespace
`helmissions` is upgraded with it: deployed, revision 2 or later, 3 Ready replicas, concurrency 16 and a readiness probe period of 5 seconds.

mission.name: GitOps Render Lost The ServiceMonitor
mission.description:
The checkout service is deployed GitOps-style: CI runs `./render.sh`, which renders the chart with `helm template`
into `rendered/prod.yaml`, and the pipeline applies that file with `kubectl apply`. The cluster has the
`ServiceMonitor` CRD (group `monitoring.helmissions.io`) and the chart's `templates/servicemonitor.yaml` is meant to
create a monitor for it. Yet there is no ServiceMonitor in the cluster, the metrics dashboard is empty, and neither
render nor apply printed a single error. `helm install` of the same chart directly on the cluster does create it.
Chart, values, `render.sh` and the rendered output are in your workspace.
mission.objective:
`./render.sh` (still based on `helm template`, no cluster needed in CI) produces `rendered/prod.yaml` that contains the ServiceMonitor
`checkout` with the 15s scrape interval from `env/prod.yaml`, and `rendered/prod.yaml` is exactly what the script emits now.
That file is applied: in namespace `helmissions` the ServiceMonitor `checkout` exists next to the Ready Deployment and Service.
The chart keeps its capability guard (rendering without the CRD's API still leaves the monitor out).

mission.name: Umbrella Down
mission.description:
The marketplace platform ships as one umbrella chart, `marketplace`, with five vendored subcharts: gateway, catalog, cart,
pricing and notifier. Nothing is deployed yet and the release does not even render:
  Error: marketplace/charts/pricing/templates/deployment.yaml:36:29
    executing "marketplace/charts/pricing/templates/deployment.yaml" at <.Values.resources.limits.cpu>:
      nil pointer evaluating interface {}.cpu
The security rule is that every image reference goes through the umbrella's single setting `global.imageRegistry`
(so the registry can be switched for all five services in one place). The chart is in `marketplace/` in your workspace.
mission.objective:
Release `marketplace` is `deployed` in namespace `helmissions` with Ready Deployments for all five services
(`marketplace-gateway`, `-catalog`, `-cart`, `-pricing`, `-notifier`). Every container image of all five starts with the
registry from `global.imageRegistry` (currently `docker.io`), and that is true because the subcharts honour the global:
rendering the umbrella with `--set global.imageRegistry=mirror.example.test` moves every image to that registry. The five
subcharts stay separate charts inside `marketplace/charts/`.

mission.name: Three Tiers Down
mission.description:
Page, 02:14: "ledger front end is returning errors". The ledger service is three Helm releases
(`ledger-db`, `ledger-api`, `ledger-web`) deployed by `deploy.sh` in your workspace. Last night's pipeline run
was never checked. `http://ledger-web/cgi-bin/balance` (from inside the cluster) does not give the healthy
answer, `helm list` shows more than one problem, and `kubectl get pods` shows pods that are not ready.
`ONCALL.md` has the architecture notes. Nobody knows which tier broke first.
mission.objective:
All three releases (`ledger-db`, `ledger-api`, `ledger-web`) are `deployed` in namespace `helmissions`, the
database schema migration hook has completed successfully for `ledger-db`, and
`http://ledger-web/cgi-bin/balance` answers `web ok -> api ok -> db pong schema=v3`. The charts and values in your
workspace are the source of truth: they must match what is running, so re-running `deploy.sh` keeps it healthy.

mission.name: Registry Moved
mission.description:
The company switched off `registry.old.internal:5000` at 01:00 and copied every shop image to the new registry
(see `MIGRATION.md`). After the cut-over, `deploy-all.sh` was run again and the shop is degraded: some pods are in
`ErrImagePull` / `ImagePullBackOff`, and even after a first round of fixes the picture does not look completely
clean. Three releases are involved (`shop-cart`, `shop-search`, `shop-media`); `shop-search` brings a vendored
subchart.
mission.objective:
Releases `shop-cart`, `shop-search` and `shop-media` are `deployed` in namespace `helmissions`, every pod (including
the search `indexer` subchart pods) is Running and Ready, and every container image comes from `localhost:5001`;
nothing references `registry.old.internal` any more. The services answer on `http://shop-cart`, `http://shop-search`
and `http://shop-media`.
What the workspace's `values/` files and charts
render must use the new registry too, so the next `deploy-all.sh` run stays healthy.

mission.name: The 50% Canary
mission.description:
The catalog 2.0 canary was supposed to see about 10% of the traffic: 9 stable pods and 1 canary pod behind the shared
`catalog` Service. Instead the dashboard shows 50/50 splits at one moment and zero canary traffic the next, the canary
release is not green, and the rollout notes in `ROLLOUT.md` say everything was deployed with `release.sh`.
`curl http://catalog/` (from inside the cluster) shows which track answered.
mission.objective:
Release `catalog-stable` runs 9 ready pods and release `catalog-canary` runs 1 ready pod, both `deployed` in namespace
`helmissions`. The Service `catalog` load-balances over all 10 pods (the canary is one of its endpoints) and real
requests to `http://catalog/` are answered by the canary some of the time but by the stable track the vast majority of
the time. What the workspace's values and chart render must say the same, so the next `release.sh` keeps the split.

mission.name: Wrong Namespace DNS
mission.description:
After the tenancy project moved the orders back end to its own namespace, the customer dashboard shows no orders:
`curl http://orders-web/cgi-bin/dashboard` (from inside `helmissions-web`) ends in a name-resolution or connection
error instead of the open order count. Both releases say `deployed`, both pods are Running and Ready. Fixing the first
obvious thing does not bring the dashboard back. The two tiers and their namespaces are described in `TEAMS.md`.
mission.objective:
Release `orders-api` is `deployed` in namespace `helmissions-api` and release `orders-web` is `deployed` in namespace
`helmissions-web`. `http://orders-web/cgi-bin/dashboard` called from `helmissions-web` shows the open orders served by
the back end that runs in namespace `helmissions-api` (not a copy in another namespace). The charts and values in the
workspace must describe the working setup (a new `deploy.sh` run keeps it healthy).

mission.name: Dev Values In Prod
mission.description:
Finance reports test invoices landing in the real ledger. The prod release `invoice` in namespace `helmissions` was
deployed by the pipeline script `deploy.sh prod` yesterday, and the config page (`http://invoice/config.txt`, from inside
the cluster) looks like the development environment: sandbox payments, debug logging and debug endpoints are on. A
first attempt at "just fixing the script" last night did not clear everything. The runbook in `RUNBOOK.md` says how prod and
dev are supposed to differ. Dev (`invoice-dev` in `helmissions-dev`) must keep working as it is.
mission.objective:
Running `bash deploy.sh prod` from the workspace leaves release `invoice` in namespace `helmissions` `deployed`, with 2 ready
pods and a config page reporting `environment=prod`, `payments=live`, `log_level=warn`, `debug_endpoints=false` and
`database=invoice-db.helmissions`. Running it again keeps it that way (the pipeline is idempotent). Release `invoice-dev`
in `helmissions-dev` is untouched: still `environment=dev` with sandbox payments and debug logging.

mission.name: Pending Forever
mission.description:
Last night's release of the telemetry platform (`bash release.sh`) ended with "timed out waiting for the condition". Three
releases (`telemetry-ingest`, `telemetry-rollup`, `telemetry-alerts`) are in state `failed`, the services still answer with
version 1.0, and `kubectl get pods -n helmissions` shows new pods stuck in `Pending` while the old ones keep running.
The scheduler's reasons differ from pod to pod. `CAPACITY.md` holds the capacity plan and the pod budgets.
mission.objective:
Releases `telemetry-ingest`, `telemetry-rollup` and `telemetry-alerts` are `deployed` in namespace `helmissions` on version
2.0 (`http://telemetry-<service>/` reports `version=2.0`): ingest and rollup run 1 ready pod each, alerts runs 2 ready pods,
no pod is Pending. Every pod keeps a CPU and a memory request within the per-pod budget in `CAPACITY.md`, and the
workspace's values files describe exactly what is running so the next `release.sh` stays green.

mission.name: Silent Pipeline Failure
mission.description:
Prod billing broke after last night's promotion run, yet the pipeline job was green. `bash pipeline.sh` in your workspace promotes a
build through dev, staging and prod (`PIPELINE.md` has the table of releases, namespaces and what each environment must look like).
The run printed `Error:` lines, then carried on to prod anyway. Release `billing` in `helmissions` is in state `failed`, a new pod is
not starting, and the old pods are the only reason billing still answers.
mission.objective:
Running `bash pipeline.sh` from the workspace succeeds and leaves all three environments `deployed` and healthy: `billing-dev` in
`helmissions-dev`, `billing-staging` in `helmissions-staging` and `billing` in `helmissions`, each serving the page described in
`PIPELINE.md` and prod running the build that staging ran. The pipeline must also stop at the first failing stage: if staging cannot be
deployed, it exits non-zero and does not touch prod.

mission.name: Unable To Build Kubernetes Objects
mission.description:
Since the cluster upgrade, every `helm upgrade` of the `edge-gateway` release fails before it changes anything with
`resource mapping not found ... no matches for kind ... in version ...`. Even `helm status` on the release is unhappy. The gateway itself is up and serving, but the 1.4.0 chart in your workspace
(see `UPGRADE-NOTES.md`) cannot be released and the change window is open. The gateway must not be removed and recreated.
mission.objective:
Release `edge-gateway` in namespace `helmissions` is `deployed` on a new revision (at least revision 3) created by upgrading the
existing release with the workspace chart, the earlier revisions are still in `helm history`, and
`http://edge-gateway/` answers `edge-gateway version=1.4 rate_limit=200`. The release's current manifest and the workspace chart
use only API versions the cluster serves, the PodDisruptionBudget and HorizontalPodAutoscaler exist with sane settings
(autoscaling between 2 and 4 replicas) and the gateway has 2 or more ready pods.

mission.name: Two Teams, One ClusterRole
mission.description:
Team B's rollout of the shared `collector` chart failed with `Unable to continue with install: ClusterRole "..." in namespace "" exists
and cannot be imported into the current release: invalid ownership metadata`. The same chart has been running for team A for weeks in its own
namespace. Both teams need their own collector, in their own namespace, each with its own access to the pod list. Beware: the first error is
rarely the last one for a chart written for a single tenant. `TEAMS.md` lists the releases, namespaces and values files.
mission.objective:
Releases `team-a` (namespace `helmissions-team-a`) and `team-b` (namespace `helmissions-team-b`) are both `deployed` from the chart in the
workspace. They share no cluster-scoped object: every ClusterRole, ClusterRoleBinding and PriorityClass in one release's manifest has a name
that is scoped to its own release (contains the release name or its namespace), each is owned by its own release, and each collector's
ServiceAccount is really allowed to list pods (`http://team-a-collector/status` in `helmissions-team-a` and `http://team-b-collector/status`
in `helmissions-team-b` report `pods-api=200`). The chart must render the same shape for any release name and namespace.

mission.name: The Final Incident
mission.description:
INC-4471: Tideline 2.0 has to be live in staging and prod before the 15:00 freeze, and nothing about the release is clean. The
prod deploy was killed mid-run by the CI runner, and every `helm upgrade` of `tideline` has been refused since. Staging was deployed
earlier today and QA says it "feels wrong". The umbrella chart pulls a `cache` dependency from the internal chart registry, and the
status pages (`http://tideline/cgi-bin/status` in `helmissions`, `http://tideline-staging/cgi-bin/status` in `helmissions-staging`) do
not look like the healthy answer described in `INCIDENT.md`. You have the whole pipeline in your workspace. Work like the on-call engineer
you are: several things are wrong at once, and they hide each other.
mission.objective:
Both environments run Tideline 2.0 from the workspace and are healthy. Release `tideline` (prod, namespace `helmissions`) and release
`tideline-staging` (namespace `helmissions-staging`) are `deployed`, prod's newest revision is a finished upgrade (nothing stuck in a pending state), and each
environment's database-migration hook has run to completion. Each status page reports `status=ok`, schema `13`, cache `1.2.x`
and a database host that belongs to its own environment (`tideline-db.<its namespace>`). The chart's dependencies in the workspace are consistent
(`helm dependency list` reports `ok`), and `bash deploy.sh staging` followed by `bash deploy.sh prod` run cleanly from the workspace.
